name: Astrophysics & Observational Cosmology
description: Citation network of milestone discoveries in gravitational waves, black holes, and cosmic expansion.

nodes.title: Observation of Gravitational Waves from Binary Black Hole Merger
nodes.abstract: The Advanced LIGO interferometers detected a transient gravitational-wave signal produced by the coalescence of two stellar-mass black holes, confirming Einstein general relativity in the strong-field dynamical regime.

nodes.title: First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results: Shadow of a Black Hole
nodes.abstract: Using a global sub-millimeter very-long-baseline interferometer array, the EHT reconstructed the first direct image of the supermassive black hole shadow in the center of the giant elliptical galaxy M87.

nodes.title: Observational Evidence for an Accelerating Universe and Dark Energy
nodes.abstract: Observations of 16 high-redshift Type Ia supernovae demonstrate that the cosmic expansion is currently accelerating, providing direct evidence for a non-zero cosmological constant or dark energy component.

nodes.title: A Jupiter-Mass Companion to a Solar-Type Star (First Exoplanet)
nodes.abstract: We report the discovery of a planetary companion orbiting the solar-type star 51 Pegasi, detected via high-precision Doppler radial velocity shifts, initiating the era of observational exoplanetary astronomy.

nodes.title: Inflationary Universe: A Possible Solution to Horizon Problems
nodes.abstract: We propose an inflationary model of the early universe where an exponential supercooled expansion solves the horizon, flatness, and magnetic monopole cosmological problems within grand unified field theories.

nodes.title: The Foundation of the General Theory of Relativity (Einstein)
nodes.abstract: We formulate the field equations of general relativity, establishing that gravity is not a Newtonian force but geometric curvature of four-dimensional spacetime induced by mass and energy distribution.

nodes.title: Measurements of Omega and Lambda from 42 High-Redshift Supernovae
nodes.abstract: The Supernova Cosmology Project confirms the accelerated expansion of the universe, constraining matter density and vacuum energy density parameters to favor an open or spatially flat cosmological geometry.

nodes.title: Planck 2018 Results: Cosmological Parameters
nodes.abstract: High-precision full-sky measurements of the cosmic microwave background temperature and polarization anisotropies by the Planck satellite determine fundamental cosmological parameters of the standard Lambda-CDM model.
